# Area audit: the numbers are right

Step 2.109. Area 6 of [LEADS.md](../LEADS.md): "Players, coaches and parents who will argue about them. Scores, fouls, clocks, standings, tie-breaks, statistics, corrections and history are right in every case, and say why when a rule decided them."

Written 2026-11-16 by the area lead for the numbers, from build branch commit `df2074c`. It changes no code, no test and no plan.

## The first test, in plain words

The founder's walk (a new season on the default rules, two teams, one game scored live with an Undo and ended in the middle of the second half, one game whose final score was typed) gives **the right score, the right points and fouls for every player, the right team totals, the right standings and the right order of the two teams**. Every number the product shows in that walk was worked by hand and matched (section 1).

What the founder would notice:

1. **Minutes are missing.** The engine counts every player's minutes correctly (30:00, 3:00, 27:00 and so on), and the default season keeps minutes, but no public page shows them: not the game's box score, not the statistics page (finding M1). This is a missing number, and it is the one step below marked (TEST 1).
2. **A puzzling sentence under the table.** Both teams level on wins carry the note "Placed above the teams level with it by the difference between points scored and allowed", including the team that was placed below (M2).
3. **Puzzling per-game numbers.** The statistics page says Ravens score 7.0 points a game, while the standings say 52 points in 2 games: statistics count only the game that has a box score, as the spec says (P7 section 8), but the page never says so (M5).
4. **No leaders after one game.** "No leaders yet" and "A player needs at least 3 games to be ranked": right by S-63, and the page says why. `first-test.md` (step 2.194) should say it too, or the walk should set the minimum to 1.

No number in the walk is wrong. One number is missing.

## How this was done, and what was not checked

- **Read in full:** the engine (`packages/sports/src/basketball/live.ts`), the standings (`packages/sports/src/standings`) and statistics (`packages/sports/src/stats`) maths and their tests, the server half that turns plays into lines and results (`packages/core/src/modules/games`: `live-game.ts`, `finish-tracked-game.ts`, `apply-tracker-commands.ts`, `record-final-score.ts`, `record-forfeit.ts`, `set-box-score.ts`, `decide-game.ts`, `read-game-page.ts`), the standings module (`packages/core/src/modules/standings`), the page builders (`apps/web/src/features/stats-pages`, `apps/web/src/features/live-game`), P7, T6, T3 section 9 and the S-decisions.
- **Run, not just read:** every case below marked "run" was played through the product's own core commands (`openScoringSession`, `applyTrackerCommands` with the tracker's protocol, `recordFinalScore`, `recordForfeit`, `setBoxScore`, `reopenGame`, `postponeGame`, `cancelGame`, `addAdjustment`) on the stand-in's made-up world (`testWorld`, the same rows and the same event handlers the local app uses), and read back through the same functions the public pages call (`readStandings` and `buildStandingsViews`, `loadStatsPage`, `loadHomeLeaders`, `readGamePage`, `buildBoxScores`, `buildPlays`). The scripts were one-off test files in my scratch space, outside the repository; none is kept. Engine cases were run on the engine with the rules the server hands it (`engineRulesOf(defaultSeasonRules())`).
- **Pictured:** `node scripts/shots.mjs --dev --only=game-final,standings,stats` (pictures in `.local/shots`, which git ignores): the made-up North Valley league's standings, statistics and a final game scored by the tracker; Harbor City's standings. Its two tables were then worked by hand from the seed's games (cases 45 to 47).
- **Not checked:** the walk in a browser. No made-up league starts empty until step 2.192, and Undo and End game on the new scoring screen are step 2.37; the numbers were judged through the engine and the server's commands, as the brief asked. The database's stores (PGlite) were not run: only the stand-in. The live updates a viewer gets mid-game were read, not run. A clock that is set (S-71, step 2.189) was left alone: every game here runs its clock without a set. The box score grid's own rule for empty boxes (P7 section 5.2) lives in the form; the cases passed lines straight to the command. When the dev server first started, Next.js printed an upgrade recommendation and stopped; nothing it suggested was run.

## 1. The first-test walk, worked by hand

**The league.** One season on `defaultSeasonRules()`: two halves of 20:00, overtime 5:00, a running clock, bonus at 7 team fouls and double bonus at 10 in a half, out at 5 personal fouls, win percentage, tiebreakers head-to-head then point difference then points scored, no ties, forfeits 20 to 0 not counted in the difference, statistics "standard" (points, 3-pointers, free throws, fouls, minutes), leaders from 3 games (S-63). Ravens (players R1 to R7, numbers 1 to 7) and Wolves (W1 to W7, numbers 11 to 17). Game 1, Wolves at Ravens, scored live. Game 2, a week later, Ravens at Wolves, typed in as 50 to 45 for Wolves.

**Game 1, as tapped** (seconds from tip-off; the clock reads 20:00 less the time it has run in the half):

## 2. What is finished

Each of these is built, on the build branch, and gave the hand-worked answer in every case below.

- **The engine's numbers** (`packages/sports/src/basketball/live.ts`): scores, Undo and Redo of any play, personal and team fouls, the bonus and double bonus with the reset at the half and overtime carrying the second half's count, the foul limit's mark, a stop clock and a running clock, the mercy rule switching and switching again (S-30, S-31), the last-minutes stop clock (S-28, S-29), the clock stopping at 0:00 and waiting for the next period (S-65), overtime, and minutes on a clock that is never set.
- **What the server makes of the plays** (`packages/core/src/modules/games`): each player's line (points, 1s, 2s, 3s, fouls, turnovers, whole seconds), a "did not play" line for everyone on the roster who never came on, the final score, a level score refused without ties ("Play overtime."), a typed score refused over a game with plays (S-46).
- **Standings** (`packages/sports/src/standings`, `packages/core/src/modules/standings`): from final and forfeit games only (S-9, S-11), win percentage with a tie as half a win, points per win, tie and loss, the admin's tiebreakers in order with the restart for teams still level, forfeits at the league's score in or out of the difference, the streak, adjustments with their reasons as footnotes (S-10), a table per division counting games across divisions, and every result followed at once, corrections included.
- **Statistics** (`packages/sports/src/stats`, `statistics-source.ts`): totals and per-game averages worked only over the games where each statistic was kept (P7 section 8), no game played for a player who never came on, the league's minimum games for leaders (S-63) with every player still in the table, no leaders for fouls (S-48), a staff-only team shown as totals only (S-22), a box score saved again as a final score losing its lines (S-27).
- **The public pages**: standings with seeds and footnotes, statistics with leaders and both tables, a game's scoreboard, box scores and play-by-play, the home page's small table and leaders, each team's record and seed.

## 3. What is not finished

- **Minutes on any public page** (M1): in no plan.
- **Overtime on a result** (M8) and **the standings columns the season chooses** (M7): in no plan.
- **Adjustments, corrections and coin flips on a screen**: Admin, "Standings and stats" says "Not ready yet" (step 2.56); the season's rules are not on a screen yet (step 2.47). A coin flip has nowhere to be stored (record 030), so teams level after every tiebreaker share a rank and take seeds in a fixed order.
- **Player pages** (P7 section 6: this season, past seasons, career totals): the address exists and draws a placeholder.
- **Known and planned elsewhere, not audited again here**: team fouls reset "each half" in quarters or "once a game" (the 2.107 audit's M8, step 2.123); a reopened game's page saying it has not started (S-47, step 2.159); minutes when the clock is set (S-71, step 2.189); Undo, the play log and End game on the new scoring screen (step 2.37).

## 4. Findings

Each has its severity, its proof, what the spec says, and the step proposed for it (section 7).

### High

**H1. A box score's team total leaves out turnovers charged to the team.**

- _What a coach sees:_ North Valley's final game, Lions at Hawks (picture `north-valley-game-final`, 1280 wide): the play-by-play says "Turnover by Lions" at 19:12 of the second half; the Lions' box score Total says TO 0.
- _Proof:_ case 18 (run): one turnover charged to the team and one to a player. The engine's team count is 2; the players' lines add to 1; the page's total is the lines' sum. `packages/core/src/modules/games/queries/read-game-page.ts`, lines 226 to 233, totals the players' lines only, and a team turnover is in no line (`live-game.ts`, `linesOf`, writes players only). The statistics page's team totals (`list-team-stat-totals.ts`) are summed from the same lines, so a season keeping the full set (S-25) has the same gap.
- _Spec:_ P7 section 5.3 (both teams' box scores); T-128 ("a box score can always be explained": here the play log says 1 and the total says 0).
- No turnover is tapped in the first-test walk, so it is not (TEST 1). Step N2.

### Medium

**M1. Minutes are on no public page. (TEST 1)**

- _Proof:_ walk case 3 and case 44 (run): every minute is right in the saved lines and shown nowhere. The game's box score passes each player's counts and never their seconds (`apps/web/src/features/live-game/build-game.ts`, line 223); the statistics page's columns are the season's statistic keys (`apps/web/src/features/stats-pages/build-stats.ts`, line 226), and minutes are kept apart from those keys (`packages/core/src/modules/games/box-score-columns.ts`, line 25), so no season ever shows them; the live game's player list shows points and fouls only. No test looks for them.
- _Spec:_ P7 section 1 ("Statistics kept", default: points, 3-pointers, free throws, fouls, minutes) and section 6 ("season totals and per-game averages for every stat the season keeps"). S-71 was decided because "a coach checks minutes against the scoreboard", and step 2.189 (TEST 1) corrects minutes that nobody but the scorekeeper can read.
- Step N1.

**M2. The note that says why teams are ordered tells the lower team it was "placed above".**

- _Proof:_ walk case 7 (the Ravens, second, carry "Placed above the teams level with it by the difference between points scored and allowed"); cases 30 and 31 (the last of three teams level carries the same sentence); the North Valley picture (Falcons, Tigers and Bears each carry "Placed above…" while below the team they were level with). Every part of a split group gets the same `decidedBy` (`packages/sports/src/standings/order-teams.ts`, line 156) and the page hangs one sentence on all of them (`build-standings.ts`, line 99). The page test only checks that the sentence is there (`stats-pages.test.ts`, line 62).
- _Spec:_ S-9 ("the page can show why one is ahead"). The order itself is right in every case.
- Step N3.

**M3. Leaders: two numbers that read the same are ranked 1 and 2, and the games shown are not the games averaged.**

- _Proof:_ case 39 (run): 22 points in 3 games (7.33) and 29 in 4 (7.25) both read 7.3; the board says "1. … 7.3", "2. … 7.3", and the number card names the first alone as the leader. Case 41 (run): 3-pointers kept in 1 of a player's 2 games: the board reads "2.0" beside "2 games", the average being over 1.
- `packages/sports/src/stats/leaders.ts`, lines 15 to 19, leaves "which games the minimum counts" for "the founder to confirm"; core counts games played (`read-stat-leaders.ts`, line 51), and no decision in `DECISIONS.md` records the choice. S-63's own reason ("one or two games should not put a player at the top") argues for the games where the statistic was recorded.
- Step N6 (a decision for the lead, then a small change).

**M4. Head-to-head among three or more teams can put a team above teams it never played, the rule is in no decision, and the page does not say which games decided it.**

- _Proof:_ case 46 (North Valley West, as seeded): Lions, Tigers, Hawks and Bears all 1–1. Lions beat Bears; Tigers and Hawks split their two games; Lions never played Tigers or Hawks. The table puts Lions second, above Tigers and Hawks, "by the games they played against each other".
- _Spec:_ P7 section 1 says only "head-to-head". T3 section 9 (line 155) records the reading built in step 2.7: head-to-head "is passed over unless every one of them has played at least one of the others". That is a product rule written down only as a technical reading. It is a fair one (it counts every game the level teams played among themselves, as the professional leagues do), and the stricter reading (head-to-head only when every two of them have met) is no better here: it would put the Bears above the Lions, who beat them. Either way a parent will argue, so the rule must be a decision and the note must name the games: "Lions: 1–0 against the teams level with them".
- Step N4 (a decision for the lead, then the note).

**M5. The statistics never say what they count.**

- _Proof:_ walk case 8: the Teams table says Ravens 7.0 points a game and every player GP 1, while the standings say 52 points in 2 games. The North Valley picture: Hawks 15.0 and Lions 10.0 points a game beside 114 and 109 points in 3 games in the standings. Case 41: an average over the games a column was kept in.
- _Spec:_ right by P7 section 8 and T6 section 9 ("statistics count only the games where they were recorded"); the page never says so, and a parent compares the two pages.
- Step N5.

**M6. An adjustment can leave a record that does not add up, and nothing pairs the two sides of an overturned result.**

- _Proof:_ North Valley's Badgers (picture; case 46): GP 3, W 0, L 2, footnote "Adjusted by -1 win. Played an ineligible player in round 3." The game is now neither a win nor a loss, the percentage is worked over 2 games, and the opponent gains nothing. The made-up story is also wrong: the Badgers lost their round 3 game (Falcons 61–55), so there was no win to take away. Case 29 (run): a win awarded by ruling gives GP 2, W 2, L 1.
- _Spec:_ S-10. `packages/sports/src/standings/types.ts`, lines 54 to 60, says an overturned result is two adjustments, one per team; no command or screen makes them together (step 2.56 is not built).
- Step N9.

**M7. The standings page ignores the season's choice of columns.**

- _Proof:_ walk case 6: the default columns are GP, W, L, PCT and DIFF (`defaultSeasonRules`); the page always draws GP, W, L, PCT, PF, PA, DIFF and STRK, adding T when any game was tied and PTS when the table ranks by points (`build-standings.ts`, lines 35 to 50). Nothing in the code reads `standings.columns`, and the "last five" column the contract offers is drawn nowhere.
- _Spec:_ P7 section 1 ("which columns show"); P5 ("which columns").
- Step N7.

**M8. Overtime is not shown on the result.**

- _Proof:_ case 44 (run): level at the end of regulation, End game refused ("Play overtime."), won in the first overtime. The game's board says "Final" and nothing more (`live-game-view.tsx`, lines 264 to 268, draws no period once a game is not live); the result cards on the schedule, the home page and the standings read a public game that carries no periods (`stand-in-world-reads.ts`, lines 73 to 101). Only the play-by-play's heading, "OT1", says it.
- _Spec:_ P7 section 5.6 ("Overtime: added periods; shown on the result").
- Step N8.

**M9. A typed score that differs from the players' points shows a Total that does not match the score.**

- _Proof:_ case 40 (run): typed 50, the players' points add to 48. The board says 50, the box score's Total 48, the statistics' team total 48, the standings 50; nothing says where 2 points went.
- _Spec:_ S-26 keeps the typed score, rightly. The public page should account for the difference.
- Step N10.

### Low

- **L1.** A "leader" with nothing: the statistics page lists players at 0 on a board (case 40: three players "1." at 0), and gives a number card to a player who leads alone with 0 (case 37: "3-pointers made leader … 0"). The home page already leaves out leaders at 0 (`build-home-leaders.ts`, line 125). Step N6.
- **L2.** The Team column names a team a player never played for: a player who left Ash before its first game and scored for Birch reads "Birch, Ash" (case 36), because the links include roster places (`list-player-team-links.ts`). They are needed for privacy; the column should use teams with a line. Step N5.
- **L3.** Percentages are written 0.500 and 1.000 (`build-standings.ts`, line 17); a basketball table writes .500 and 1.000. A team with no games shows 0.000 (case 34). Step N7.
- **L4.** A team with no games sits above a winless team "by point difference" (case 34): right by the rules (none lost against one lost), and N3's wording makes it read naturally. Step N3.
- **L5.** A player who did not play has a dash in every column and no words (walk case 4; "Fay Lionel" in the North Valley picture). P7 section 5.6. Step N10.
- **L6.** A player at the foul limit is marked in the engine (case 12) but not on the public box score, where T-128 places the mark ("marked out in their box score line"). Step N10.
- **L7.** The game's box score shows TO in a season that keeps the standard set, which has no turnovers, while the statistics page does not (walk case 2): the columns follow the lines, not the season's "Statistics kept" (`build-game.ts`, lines 195 to 210). Step N10.
- **L8.** The home page's small table (GP, W, L, PCT) carries the note "by the difference between points scored and allowed" without the difference column (`home-page.tsx`, line 25). Step N7.
- **L9.** S-47 says "What the standings do meanwhile is unchanged (S-11)"; the product, as T-250 says, takes a reopened game out of the table until it is final again (case 27: 2 played becomes 1). The decision's words should say that. For the lead's next edit of `DECISIONS.md`.
- **L10.** Teams level after every tiebreaker take seeds in a fixed order (Harbor City: Rockets 2, Meteors 3; case 47), and no coin flip can be recorded (record 030). The note says so. Before a bracket seeds from the table (S-4), the coin flip needs its store and its screen. For step 2.56's or 2.47's line.
- **L11.** In the first-test walk the statistics page will say "No leaders yet": right by S-63 (3 games), and the page says why, but `first-test.md` should say it too, or the walk should set League settings' minimum to 1 first. One line for step 2.194.

## 5. The cases

"Run" means played through the product (the engine for cases 9 to 20; core's commands on the made-up world, read back through the pages' own builders, for 21 to 44). Default rules unless a case says otherwise. Cases 1 to 8 are the first-test walk, in section 1.

## 6. Rules in the spec that no test covers

Searched in `packages/sports`, `packages/core`, `apps/web` and `tests/`.

1. Minutes on a game's box score and on the statistics page (P7 sections 1 and 6): not built, no test (M1).
2. Overtime shown on the result (P7 section 5.6): only the play-by-play's period names are tested (`game-words.test.ts`, line 15) (M8).
3. Which standings columns show (P7 section 1): nothing reads the setting (M7).
4. Why each team is where it is (S-9): the page test checks that a sentence is present, not that it is true for the team it is beside (M2).
5. Turnovers charged to the team in the team's totals (P7 section 5.3; S-25 for the season's team totals) (H1).
6. Head-to-head among three or more level teams who met in separate pairs (M4): `order-teams.test.ts`, line 45, tests only a team that met none of the others.
7. Leaders whose written numbers are equal but whose ranks differ, and a leader at 0 on the statistics page (M3, L1).
8. The first-test walk's numbers end to end at the level of the pages: each piece is tested alone, and step 2.194's browser test is not written yet. The scripts this audit ran show it can be a fast test (N1's done test).
9. A typed score against its players' points on the public page (S-26): the grid's warning is tested, the page is not (M9).

## 7. Proposed steps

The lead numbers them, adds them, or writes in the log why not. Only N1 meets the first-test line's bar (a missing number the founder would see in the walk).

- **N1 (TEST 1). Minutes on the game page and the statistics page (M1).** For coaches, players and parents who check minutes, and for the founder's first test (step 2.189 corrects minutes no one can read today). The game's box score gets a minutes column (m:ss, rounded down as the tracker rounds) for a game whose lines carry minutes (every live game; a box score where they were typed), and none where none were kept; the statistics page shows minutes per game (over the games where minutes were kept) and in total, for seasons that keep them ("standard" and "full"); the words in the message files. With it, one fast test that plays the first-test walk through core's commands on the made-up world and reads the pages' own builders, pinning every number in section 1 of this audit, so a change that moves one is seen at once. _Spec: P7 sections 1, 5.3 and 6; S-71. Needs: nothing new (it reads the saved lines, so it goes with 2.189 in either order). Folders: `apps/web/src/features/live-game`, `apps/web/src/features/stats-pages`, `packages/ui/src/box-score-table`, `packages/site/src/messages`, `apps/web/src/server` (the test). Done test: the walk's game page shows R1 30:00, R3 3:00, R6 27:00, W2 22:00, W6 8:00 and no minutes for R7 and W7; its statistics page the same per game; a season keeping points only shows no minutes column; pictures at 390 and 1280; the fast walk test passes; the area 6 lead has checked the pictures against section 1. Model: opus, high._
- **N2. Team turnovers in team totals (H1).** For coaches reading a box score. A game's Total counts turnovers charged to the team (from the saved state, or a team line: the builder's choice, said in a record), and the season's team totals do the same. _Spec: P7 section 5.3; S-25; T-128. Folders: `packages/core/src/modules/games/queries`, `packages/core/src/modules/standings`, `packages/database/src/queries`. Done test: case 18 gives a Total of 2; North Valley's Lions show TO 1 in the picture; a unit test of the game page with a team turnover. Model: sonnet._
- **N3. The note under the standings true for every team (M2, L4).** For a parent of the team placed second. A sentence that is true for each place it is beside, for example "Level on record with the Wolves; ordered by point difference." or one sentence per tied group ("Wolves and Ravens are level on record; point difference puts the Wolves first."). _Spec: S-9. Folders: `apps/web/src/features/stats-pages`, `packages/core/src/modules/standings/queries`, `packages/site/src/messages`. Done test: the walk's table, cases 30 and 31, and the North Valley East picture each read true for every team; the page test checks the sentence beside the lower team. Model: sonnet._
- **N4. Head-to-head among three or more, decided and explained (M4).** For every team in a multi-way tie. The lead records the rule as a product decision ("decided for you" in `DECISIONS.md`, with T3 section 9 pointing to it). Recommended: keep today's reading (the games the level teams played among themselves all count, so a game one of them won is never ignored), and offer the stricter reading as a season setting only when a league asks. Then the note beside each team placed by head-to-head names its record in those games ("Lions: 1–0 against the teams level with them"), which needs core's standings read to carry it. No change under `packages/sports`. Could join N3. _Spec: P7 section 1; S-9. Folders: `docs/specs/v1`, `packages/core/src/modules/standings`, `apps/web/src/features/stats-pages`, `packages/site/src/messages`. Done test: the North Valley West notes read true for Lions, Tigers, Hawks and Bears; cases 31 to 33 unchanged; a new order test for level teams who met in separate pairs. Model: sonnet._
- **N5. The statistics say what they count (M5, L2).** For a parent comparing the statistics with the standings. The Teams table shows how many games its numbers come from beside the team's games played ("1 of 2 games"), and one sentence under both tables says that statistics count only games with a box score; the Team column lists only teams the player has a line for. _Spec: P7 section 8; T6 section 9. Done test: the walk's Ravens read 7.0 "from 1 of 2 games"; case 36's second player reads Birch only; pictures. Model: sonnet._

### For the founder, in plain words

The scores, fouls, standings and statistics the product works out are right in every case I tried by hand: 47 of them, from a one-point game to three teams level and a game corrected after it ended. What is not right yet is what the pages show: minutes are counted but shown nowhere, the note under a tied table tells the second team it was "placed above", a team turnover is left out of a box score's total, overtime is not shown on a result, and the statistics page does not say it counts only games with box scores. One rule needs writing down: when three or more teams are level, head-to-head counts the games they played among themselves, so a team can finish above another it never played (the Lions above the Tigers in the made-up league, because the Lions beat the Bears). I recommend keeping that rule, recording it as decided for you, and having the page name the games that decided it; the lead will give it a decision number you can quote to change it.
